run.change_description: [field] Sync controlled value changes with field state

summary.intent: Give Field.Control one owner per value-source: `useValueChanged` drives dirty/filled/validity for the controlled path (mirroring Combobox, Number Field, Select, and OTP Field), and the DOM `onChange` handler drives them only when uncontrolled, replacing the two sync paths that previously both ran. This fixes a numeric/array dirty-state comparison bug (string DOM value vs. non-string captured baseline), makes programmatic controlled-value changes update filled/dirty/validity, honors `details.cancel()` from `onValueChange` on the uncontrolled path, and keeps a controlled value the consumer rejects or rewrites from reaching field state. Intent source: the caller-supplied PR description (`spec-pr-5460`); the single commit message carries no further detail.
summary.issue_fit: No originating issue; the supplied PR description is the only intent source. Its four described fixes (numeric/array dirty baseline, programmatic-change staleness, `details.cancel()`, rejected/rewritten controlled values) are each implemented and covered by a passing added test, or directly evident from the diff. The performance table's `onSubmit` render count is confirmed by an added test; its `onChange`-mode number is a plausible but untested supporting assertion.
summary.coverage: Both changed files reviewed in full (`FieldControl.tsx` +48/-20, `FieldControl.test.tsx` +149/-6); no other file in the 2-file diff. Ran the full existing suite at head (`FieldControl.test.tsx`, 26 passed/1 skipped) and, to falsify a suspected regression, an independent scratch jsdom test comparing head against the merge-base version of the one changed source file (everything else identical) — see finding `field-control/filled-not-cleared-on-remount`, confirmed by an independent fresh-context verifier. No other candidates survived falsification.

findings.title: Mount effect never clears data-filled when a Field.Control remounts empty
findings.trigger: A Field.Root stays mounted while its Field.Control child is swapped for a different control instance (a different `key`, or a conditionally rendered different control) whose initial value is empty, after the previous control instance had left the field filled.
findings.impact: `data-filled` (and the `filled` field of Field.Root's public state) stays stuck `true` on the new, empty control. Reproduced directly: mounting `Field.Root` > `Field.Control key="a" value="foo"` then swapping to `Field.Control key="b" value=""` leaves `data-filled` present at head, where the merge-base's version of the same file clears it. `filled` is documented public field state (`FieldRootState.filled`, "Whether the field has a value"), so this is user-visible, e.g. through floating-label or empty-state styling driven by `data-filled`.
findings.change: Make the mount-time effect symmetric so it also clears `filled` to `false` when the current DOM value is empty, matching the effect it replaced (`else if (hasExternalValue && valueProp === '') setFilled(false)`), e.g. `setFilled(!!validation.inputRef.current?.value)` unconditionally instead of only inside the truthy branch.

requirements.source: spec-pr-5460/"With value={5} the baseline was the number 5, so \"5\" !== 5 held forever...The control now registers the serialized value"
requirements.evidence: FieldControl.tsx computes `serializedValue = value == null ? undefined : String(value)` and registers/compares that string consistently; test `clears dirty state when a numeric controlled value returns to its initial value` passes at head (part of the 26-passed run below).

requirements.source: spec-pr-5460/"Programmatic changes left the field stale...updated the input text but not filled, dirty, or validity"
requirements.evidence: `useValueChanged(serializedValue, ...)` now runs `clearErrors`, `setDirty`, `setFilled`, and `validation.change` on every controlled value change regardless of source; test `syncs state and validates when the controlled value changes programmatically` passes at head.

requirements.source: spec-pr-5460/"details.cancel() in onValueChange now stops the internal handling. It was ignored."
requirements.evidence: The uncontrolled `onChange` handler now guards with `!details.isCanceled` before `clearErrors`/`validation.change`; test `does not validate when the change is canceled` passes at head.

requirements.source: spec-pr-5460/"A controlled value the consumer rejects or rewrites no longer reaches the field state, matching Combobox, Number Field and OTP Field."
requirements.evidence: `onChange` returns immediately after calling `onValueChange` when `isControlled`, before any `setDirty`/`setFilled`/`validation.change`, so field state only ever reflects what the consumer feeds back through the `value` prop.

requirements.source: spec-pr-5460/"Renders per keystroke...onSubmit: 1 per keystroke (Base) vs 2 on the first, then 1 (This PR)"
requirements.evidence: Test `renders once per keystroke for controlled input changes` (default `onSubmit` validation mode) asserts exactly one extra render per keystroke after the first, matching the claimed steady state; passes at head.

requirements.source: spec-pr-5460/"onChange: 1 per keystroke (Base) vs 2 per keystroke (This PR)"
requirements.evidence: No added test exercises `validationMode="onChange"` render counts for a controlled input; the mechanism described (an extra render from the layout-effect-driven state update) is plausible and consistent with the `onSubmit` measurement that was verified, but the specific number is not independently confirmed here.
